subject: Urgent: CloudRetail launch capacity surge — elevated 5xx/429 and retry behavior
messages:
From: Bethany Cole <bethany@cloudretail.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-01T08:12:05-07:00
Subject: Launch traffic — seeing 429 / 5xx spike

Vanessa,

We went live with the new home-page personalization at 08:00 PT and immediately started seeing large numbers of 429s and intermittent 5xx responses for our API calls to Redwood. Our users are experiencing timeouts and repeated retries; Ive attached a screenshot of the most frequent error and a short tail of the logs from our side (ops@cloudretail.com). Traffic is roughly 8x our planned steady-state for the first 30 minutes.

Can you confirm whether this is a rate-limit, autoscaler lag, or something else on Redwood's side? We need a quick workaround; our product team is pressuring us for a rollback window.

- Bethany

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-01T08:35:44-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch traffic — seeing 429 / 5xx spike

Im looking at the realtime dashboard: the autoscaler has fired additional nodes but the backend queue depth for the large seq-length model is increasing. Were hitting two correlated issues: (1) request fanout + long-tail model latency causing receptor queueing, and (2) aggressive client retry loops causing amplified load and 429s.

Short-term remedial suggestions:
- Switch the customer's default model route to the fast-variant (lower latency, smaller context) for the next 30 minutes (helps cut CPU cycles).
- Turn on transient 30s retry-backoff (on our rate-limiter) to provide backpressure to clients.
- Temporarily raise the per-customer concurrency cap by 2x for CloudRetail (manual override).

Ill open a quick patch to change the route and prepare a config change for concurrency caps. Need SRE to push the rate-limiter change.

Jonas Weber
Director, Product Platform
Redwood Inference

Related: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/uptime?view=cloudretail-launch
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-01T08:50:09-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Launch traffic — seeing 429 / 5xx spike

Observed in infra: large number of clients hitting our 429 path which then immediately retry with minimal backoff (per CloudRetail logs). That creates a retry storm — the retries are the dominant traffic during the surge window, not fresh user requests. Also seeing a small number of 5xx spikes from a specific inference cluster (cluster-a1) that triggered transient failovers. I recommend: 

Steps we can take right now (actionable):
1) Apply a temporary server-side client throttle for CloudRetail: set rate-limit to 60rps with standard exponential backoff headers. Command: `rbctl apply-policy --customer CLD-4721 --policy temp-throttle-60rps --duration 120m`
2) Deploy the route switch to `model-fast-v2` (Jonas to seed).
3) Re-route 10% of traffic to older model variant as a safety fallback (low-latency but lower quality).
4) Rotate cluster-a1 and force a rolling restart of the worker pool (I can run the job now).

Im starting the cluster restart and will push the throttle policy in the next 5m. Ill attach the tail of the error logs.

Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference

Attachments: server-logs-0601-tail.txt
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Bethany Cole <bethany@cloudretail.com>
Cc: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-06-01T09:05:21-07:00
Subject: Re: Launch traffic — seeing 429 / 5xx spike

Hi Bethany — thanks for the quick flag and the logs. Weve implemented a short-term mitigation plan: 
- Server-side throttle applied (60 rps) and Exponential Backoff headers enabled.
- Routing switched to `model-fast-v2` for CloudRetail.
- Rolling restart of cluster-a1 is in-progress (Rishi).

Could you please ask your client engineers to increase retry backoff to 30s max and disable aggressive immediate retries for the next 2 hours? That will help the throttle be effective. Were monitoring and will confirm when 429/5xx rates normalize.

I know your product team is watching closely — were treating this as high priority and will follow up with a postmortem.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Subject: Escalation: CloudRetail launch incident — request for exec attention and credit

Marissa / Leadership,

FYI: CloudRetail (CLD-4721) experienced a launch-time capacity surge at ~08:00 PT that resulted in a combination of retry storms, elevated 429s, and transient 5xx in cluster-a1. We applied a temporary server-side throttle, switched routing to a low-latency model variant, and restarted the impacted cluster — customer reports initial improvement but still requests confirmation on SLA credits.

Impact summary (high level):
- Duration: ~08:00	 08:45 PT most severe; tail effects to ~09:20 PT.
- Visible effects: increased 429 rate, amplified retries from client side, a handful of 5xx failovers.
- Customer asks: immediate stabilization, 48h postmortem and consideration of SLA credit.

Recommended next steps for leadership:
1) Approve a goodwill credit for the outage window while we finish the postmortem (suggested: one week's invoice credit for June).
2) Commit to a 48-hour postmortem and prioritize root-cause analysis on retry amplification and autoscaler behavior.
3) Prepare a joint customer-facing timeline and RCA.

Ill own customer comms and schedule the internal postmortem. Please advise on credit approval — the customer expects a quick answer.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
